transcript_body:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-25 14:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramirez (Redwood SE), Nia Patel (Redwood PM); Laura Price (Orion Head of Security), Ethan Cole (Cloud Architect), Priya Singh (Legal), Jamal Rossi (DevOps)

Auto-summary: Customer requires strict EU processing for EU customer PII, wants KMS escrow option for key custody, strong audit logs with 7 year retention, and RBAC/SSO integration with their IdP. Discussed routing fallbacks and subprocessors.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick around-the-room, then we'll jump into the residency and KMS piece.
[00:18] Laura (Orion): Hi, Laura here. We're mostly concerned about EU PII, we have regulators asking for zero cross-border processing unless there's contract language.
[00:27] Ethan (Orion): Ethan as well, we'll be running some inference workloads from our EU cluster and want proof that tokens/data don't leave EU.
[00:35] Diego (Redwood SE): Great. We'll walk through region routing, geofence policies, and how we integrate with customer KMS. Quick note — apologies in advance for any slurred words, I have a spotty connection.
[00:48] Maya: Yep no worries. Nia, do you want to kick off with the high level on routing?
[00:51] Nia (Redwood PM): Sure. Redwood supports policy-based routing: you can pin requests by account, by token, or by route to a region. For strict EU processing we recommend region-pinning at the account level so all traffic stays in that region unless you opt-in for fallback. Our control plane is segregated in the VPC model for Private deployments.
[01:12] Jamal (Orion): When you say VPC model, do you mean the private control plane lives in our VPC or Redwood spins up VPCs in our cloud account?
[01:20] Diego: Both options. For the private package we can deploy control plane components into your cloud account (customer-managed VPC). For dedicated we host but we can restrict egress and use regional infra. There are tradeoffs for ops overhead vs. control.
[01:35] Priya (Orion): Legally we need to see subprocessors list and where they process data, not just region names. Any third party logging or analytics that could touch PII?
[01:45] Maya: We'll share our subprocessor inventory. For hosted flows, we use a small set of telemetry providers — we can provide a mapping. For Private deployments, we minimize external subprocessors and can run audit forwarding to your SIEM.
[01:59] Laura: KMS — we need to ensure customer-held keys for EU data. What does Redwood support for KMS?
[02:06] Diego: We support customer-managed KMS and bring-your-own-key via Cloud KMS (GCP/Google), AWS KMS, and Azure Key Vault. For the escrow flow, we offer an escrow partner that holds an offsite copy under an MSA. Escrow is optional and used for long-term recovery.
[02:28] Ethan: Is the KMS operation local to the region? Example: keys for EU data must be stored in EU.
[02:33] Diego: Yes, we can bind keys to region-specific KMS instances. For the private deployment you control the KMS in your account — keys never leave the region. For hosted we can store keys in regional HSMs.
[02:45] Maya: A note on terminology — sometimes folks ask for "KMS escrow" meaning we hand a copy to an escrow provider. We also have a "split-key" option where Redwood only holds split shares which alone are insufficient to decrypt.
[02:58] Priya: That split-key sounds promising, can you explain failure scenarios?
[03:03] Diego: Sure. In split-key, the customer holds the master share, Redwood holds a sealed share, and escrow holds a recovery share. You need at least two shares to reconstruct. It reduces single-point-of-failure risk.
[03:18] (crosstalk)
[03:21] Laura: Any audit trail for key use — i.e., who requested decryption, timestamp, and consumer app? Regulators want the full chain.
[03:30] Nia: Yes, we can emit key use audit logs to your SIEM or a regional logging pipeline. Logs include request ID, model version, route, and token-level metadata.
[03:43] Jamal: What's your retention for those logs? We need 7 years for certain claims.
[03:49] Maya: Default retention is 90 days on hosted, but for enterprise/private we offer configurable retention and archival to your object store for 7+ years. That comes with additional cost and compliance attestation.
[04:02] Ethan: How do you prevent accidental model fallback to a US-run variant? We sometimes see auto-fallback in other providers when capacity is low.
[04:10] Diego: Good question. We support hard region locks — if pinned to EU, requests are rejected if no EU capacity is available instead of failing over. We also support soft fallback where it can route to an allied region under a customer policy.
[04:25] Laura: Rejection is preferable for regulatory reasons. Can you show the policy that enforces that?
[04:31] Diego: We'll share a policy snippet. It's a config flag: region_policy: {mode: "strict"} — (transcription: region policy mode strict).
[04:40] Priya: On SSO and RBAC — we need SAML-based SSO + SCIM for provisioning. Also detailed RBAC so only specific roles can access logs and keys.
[04:51] Maya: We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for user sync. RBAC supports custom roles and resource scoping down to model and project level. Key access is gated by role and audit logs are tied to identity.
[05:07] Jamal: Are access logs tamper-evident? Our auditors prefer append-only logs with checksums.
[05:13] Nia: We provide signed log streams with SHA checksums and can ship them to your immutable store (WORM) in your cloud account.
[05:23] Laura: What about subprocessors in EU — do any of your partners process data outside the region for analytics?
[05:29] Maya: We'll provide a CSV mapping. Currently telemetry is limited; most heavy processing — inference — happens on our compute in-region. Some monitoring telem goes to our analytics provider in the EU or US depending on deployment; for Private we can disable external telemetry.
[05:47] Ethan: Can we do an on-prem style pilot where you deploy the runtime in our account but control plane stays at Redwood, so we get compute locality but easier upgrades?
[05:58] Diego: That's a hybrid model we support. Compute nodes run in your cloud account within your VPC; control plane endpoints call home for management. That can satisfy locality while reducing ops burden.
[06:10] (silence)
[06:13] Priya: Legal — any standard contract language around cross-border? We need a specific clause that says no EU personal data leaves EU except per documented exception.
[06:22] Maya: We have a data processing addendum (DPA) with region commitments; we'll attach the relevant clause. If you need custom wording our legal team can propose edits.
[06:33] Priya: Ok good.
[06:36] Laura: A quick tangent — SOC2. We'd like proof of recent audit and if there were any gaps flagged in the last 12 months.
[06:44] Maya: We'll share the SOC 2 Type II report redacted for vendor details; it includes any control exceptions. Our security page also lists remediations.
[06:54] Jamal: For the perf test Diego will run, can we also include KV cache warmup scenarios? Our workloads are chatty and rely on KV cache locality.
[07:03] Diego: Absolutely; I'll include KV cache warmup and sequence-length distributions. Note: sometimes transcription shows K-V cash — apologies — it's KV cache.
[07:15] Ethan: Are there any third-party CDNs or egress that could cross borders unexpectedly?
[07:20] Diego: No CDN for inference payloads. We control egress and can restrict egress endpoints. Static assets are cached, but PII never goes to third-party CDNs unless explicitly enabled.
[07:33] (brief pause)
[07:37] Maya: Let's go through a sample flow to be clear: a EU user request hits EU ingress, pinned account forces regional routing to EU compute, keys are bound to EU KMS, operation logged to EU-only logging pipeline archived to customer's S3 in eu-west-1. If any component is out, strict policy causes request rejection.
[08:00] Laura: That flow is basically what we need. We'll want a diagram.
[08:04] Maya: We'll share a diagram and a checklist for auditors.
[08:07] Priya: About escrow — who would the escrow partner be and under what governance?
[08:13] Nia: Our default escrow partner is a third-party custodian vetted for ISO and regional compliance. They store sealed recovery shares under a triple-signature release process. We can provide the MSA and custody procedures.
[08:28] Priya: Need the escrow's jurisdiction details — if they are in the US that's a problem for EU-only keys.
[08:33] Diego: We can place escrow in EU partner for EU-bound keys. It's configurable per-customer.
[08:40] Laura: Ok good.
[08:42] Maya: Any other blocker questions from your side?
[08:46] Ethan: Just one: does Redwood's monitoring pipeline ever process raw PII for model telemetry? We prefer tokenized metadata only.
[08:55] Nia: Telemetry is metadata-level only — hashed ids, no raw PII. For Private deployments you can disable telemetry entirely.
[09:05] Jamal: On disaster recovery, what's the RTO for EU-only compute?
[09:11] Diego: We aim for regional failover within the same geo (e.g., EU West to EU North) depending on availability and your policy. With strict pinning, we won't fail to non-EU. RTO is SLA-defined for Dedicated/pvt packages, typically minutes to low hours with hot standby.
[09:31] Priya: Please share SLA language and relevant security annexes.
[09:35] Maya: Will do.
[09:38] Laura: How long will the perf test take to schedule?
[09:40] Diego: I can provision within 3 business days, run the test over two windows to cover peak/off-peak, and deliver results in about 10 days.
[09:50] (laugh)
[09:52] Maya: That sounds good. We'll coordinate via email.
[09:55] Priya: One last legal point — do you have cyber insurance limits spelled out in the DPA? Some of our contracts require minimum limits.
[10:05] Maya: Yes, the DPA references our insurance coverage; we can provide a certificate of insurance.
[10:12] Jamal: Any blockers for custom retention to 7 years?
[10:16] Nia: No technical blockers — it's an archival plus search index rehydration cost. We'll present cost numbers in the follow-up.
[10:24] Maya: Ok let's recap.
[10:27] Maya: Action items: Maya send SOC2/ISO + subprocessor CSV; Diego run region/KV perf tests and include logs; schedule VPC/KMS demo. Priya to complete questionnaire.
[10:40] Laura: Sounds good. Let's plan for the VPC demo first week of December.
[10:46] Maya: I'll propose times. Thanks everyone.
[10:49] (meeting ends)

Meeting footer: References shared — link to compliance packet (redwood.com/compliance/orion-dpa-placeholder), perf test runbook (shared by Diego), and the sample region_policy snippet.
